name: Resection Planning and Margins
title: Resection Planning and Margins
answer: Resection planning and margins concerns the preoperative and intraoperative determination of tissue to remove in cancer or other surgery, with the aim of achieving negative margins while preserving healthy function. AI assists by fusing imaging, segmenting tumor and critical structures, and proposing cut planes. In surgical robotics and navigation, this becomes a spatial plan registered to the patient. The goal is to reduce positive margin rates and avoid damage to adjacent anatomy.

sections.body: Resection planning and margins concerns the preoperative and intraoperative determination of tissue to remove in cancer or other surgery, with the aim of achieving negative margins while preserving healthy function. AI assists by fusing imaging, segmenting tumor and critical structures, and proposing cut planes. In surgical robotics and navigation, this becomes a spatial plan registered to the patient. The goal is to reduce positive margin rates and avoid damage to adjacent anatomy.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: It runs on surgical navigation workstations, robotic consoles, and hospital imaging archives. The work needs preoperative MRI, CT, or PET fused with intraoperative tracking data. Compute often includes GPU servers for segmentation and registration, plus real-time optical or electromagnetic tracking. Some systems run on dedicated hardware in the operating room, others on hospital PACS and planning software.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work is done by segmenting tumor and organs at risk from volumetric imaging, then generating a resection volume with a safety margin. Registration aligns the plan to the patient using landmarks or surface matching. During surgery, navigation displays the planned margin relative to tracked instruments, and some robotic systems constrain or guide cutting. Machine learning models are trained on annotated resections and outcomes to predict margin status.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on surgeon accountability, patient consent for AI-assisted planning, and liability when a planned margin is wrong. Product liability and wrongful death suits against AI companies exist, and this site tracks six active cases, though not all involve resection planning. Compliance pages cover software as a medical device, data privacy for imaging, and validation requirements. Provenance of training data and model versioning matter for audit and recall.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Where it is going is toward intraoperative margin assessment with optical imaging, fluorescence, or mass spectrometry fused to the plan. Real-time deformation correction will update the resection volume as tissue shifts. Predictive models may estimate functional impact of a given margin before cutting. The field is moving from static preoperative plans to closed-loop navigation that adapts during the procedure.
